stem.en: A farmer plants a field with cuttings of one rose bush. Weeks later one disease is on every plant. Why is the whole crop at risk?

text.en: Cuttings grow so fast that disease gets ahead of them.

feedback.en: Speed of growth is not the reason. Sameness is.

text.en: All the plants are copies with the same weakness.

feedback.en: Yes. Identical plants share whatever weakness their parent had.

text.en: A plant from a cutting can never grow any roots.

feedback.en: Cuttings do grow their own roots, so this is not the reason.

text.en: Fungi can only attack plants grown from cuttings.

feedback.en: Fungi can attack plants however they were grown.

explanation.en: Every cutting is genetically identical to one bush, so what harms one plant can harm them all.

hints.en: How many different kinds of plant are in the field?
Do cuttings grow roots of their own?
